contentBlocks.text: This week you mastered four exponent rules. Let's review them all!

Quick review: multiplying same-base powers adds exponents, dividing subtracts them (Day 1). Raising a power to a power multiplies exponents, and anything to the power of 0 is 1 (Day 2). A negative exponent means take the reciprocal (Day 3). You combined multiple rules in one problem (Day 4). Simplify (x²)³ · x⁻⁴ / x⁰, showing every step.
Great work this week — you mastered all four exponent rules! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review the product, quotient, power-of-a-power, zero-exponent, and negative-exponent rules
Correctly simplify (x²)³·x⁻⁴/x⁰, applying all relevant rules in sequence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child solve the combined review problem step by step.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of exponent-rule mastery!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the rule the child found hardest this week (often negative exponents) rather than requiring all four equally
Ready for more: ask the child to explain why x⁰ in the denominator doesn't change the problem at all
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four exponent rules needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: (x²)³ = x⁶. x⁶·x⁻⁴ = x². x⁰ = 1, and dividing by 1 doesn't change anything, so (x²)³·x⁻⁴/x⁰ = x².
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Algebra 1 exponent-rules standards before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
